findings.title: Cancellation of reminders is not awaited and failures are ignored
findings.body: Booking cancellation starts deleteScheduledEmailReminder / deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside forEach and never awaits them, and those helpers swallow errors. The previous code awaited prisma.workflowReminder deletes in Promise.all; that persistence was removed. On a serverless freeze after the handler returns, or if the update throws, cancelled stays unset and unscheduled reminder rows are not deleted. The scheduleEmailReminders cron will then submit those emails to SendGrid, so cancelled bookings still receive workflow reminders. SMS cancels have the same gap and no retry cron.

findings.title: Paid booking cancels return before any reminder cleanup
findings.body: When bookingToDelete.paid is true the handler refunds, marks the booking REJECTED, and returns at this line. Reminder cancellation only runs later (around the workflowReminders loop). Every paid cancellation therefore leaves WorkflowReminder rows active, including already-submitted SendGrid/Twilio sends, so the bug this PR claims to fix still happens for all paid bookings.

findings.title: immediateDelete cancels SendGrid but does not record or retry it
findings.body: If immediateDelete is set, deleteScheduledEmailReminder POSTs a SendGrid batch cancel and returns without setting cancelled or deleting the WorkflowReminder row. Success still leaves a pending cancellation in scheduled_sends until the original send time, which is the 100-cap failure this PR describes. Failure is only console.logged, so the row stays scheduled with cancelled unset and the cron will never retry. Callers cannot tell that cancellation failed. The non-immediate path also only flips cancelled, even when scheduledDate is already inside the 15-minute cron interval, so a reminder due before the next cron tick is still delivered.

findings.title: Reschedule immediately cancels SendGrid and does not wait or roll back
findings.body: Reschedule passes immediateDelete=true for every email reminder, so each reschedule of an already-submitted reminder adds a pending SendGrid cancellation until the original sendAt (up to 72 hours). Enough reschedules reproduce the 100 pending-cancellation outage the PR is fixing. The forEach is not awaited and the surrounding try/catch cannot see promise rejections. If the SendGrid call fails, the old email still sends and is not marked cancelled for the cron. Cancellation also runs before eventManager.reschedule; a failed reschedule is not rolled back, so the original booking can lose its reminders.

findings.title: Request-reschedule no longer awaits reminder removal
findings.body: requestReschedule used to await Promise.all of workflowReminder deletes after best-effort provider cancels. That await was removed. The replacement deleteScheduledEmailReminder / deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls are fired from forEach and not awaited, and email cancellation only sets cancelled when it completes. If the handler returns or the update fails, reminders stay scheduled on SendGrid/Twilio and are not flagged for the cron, so request-reschedule still sends the old workflow reminders.

findings.title: Workflow delete cancels SendGrid in the background then destroys retry state
findings.body: Deleting a workflow calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true) and deleteScheduledSMSReminder from forEach without awaiting, then immediately await workflow.deleteMany, which cascade-deletes the reminder rows, and returns. The SendGrid/Twilio calls are still in flight when the handler finishes, so a serverless runtime can abort them. immediateDelete does not set cancelled, and the rows are gone, so the cron cannot retry. A workflow with many scheduled emails can also submit more than 100 pending cancels at once and fail the same way as the original bug. The same pattern is used when a step is deleted (immediateDelete then workflowStep.delete around line 521). Disabling an event type (around line 376) also dropped the awaited reminder deletes and only fire-and-forgets the new helpers.

findings.title: One SendGrid cancel failure stalls the whole cancellation queue
findings.body: All cancelled reminders due within the next hour are cancelled in one try/catch. DB deletes are queued and only committed after every SendGrid POST succeeds. If any request throws (invalid batch id, already cancelled, or SendGrid refusing a send inside its cutoff), the catch logs and skips Promise.all, so earlier successful cancels are not deleted. The next run loads those already-cancelled batches first, they fail again, and reminders later in the list are never cancelled until the blocking row ages out. A single bad row can therefore keep other cancelled-booking emails sending for up to an hour. The same loop also submits every due cancellation at once, so more than 100 in that hour recreates the pending-cancellation cap.

findings.title: Due reminders are deleted before SendGrid is cancelled
findings.body: The cron first deleteMany's every EMAIL WorkflowReminder with scheduledDate <= now, including rows with cancelled=true, and only then looks up reminders to cancel on SendGrid. A cancelled reminder whose send time has just passed, or that the previous run failed to cancel, is removed from the database with no SendGrid cancel and no retry. If SendGrid has not yet dispatched that sendAt, the email still goes out for a cancelled or rescheduled booking.

findings.title: Scheduler still emails reminders for cancelled bookings
findings.body: The unscheduled-email query only filters method, scheduled=false, and scheduledDate within 72 hours. It does not exclude cancelled=true and does not check booking status (CANCELLED/REJECTED). Far-future reminders are not on SendGrid yet; they are only safe if the cancel path deleted the row. When that delete is skipped, races, or fails (paid cancel, unawaited delete, swallowed error), this cron creates a SendGrid batch and sets scheduled=true, so the reminder is sent anyway.

findings.title: No tests for deferred cancel, immediateDelete, or the cron
findings.body: This change replaces awaited reminder deletes with a cancelled flag, a deferred SendGrid cancel, and an immediateDelete mode, but adds no tests. There is no coverage for paid vs unpaid cancel, reschedule, workflow delete, a SendGrid error mid-batch, or a reminder already inside the cron window. Those paths are what caused reminders to keep sending, and they can regress without a failing test.
